input:
Hello,

I'm leading a UK food and culture tour. We need a meze dinner for 18 (17 clients plus me) on Thursday 22 October 2026, seating from 19:30, in a village (not a resort strip) within 45 minutes of Larnaca by coach, with coach parking. We want the real village experience, not the tourist version: a full meze of many small courses including meat, and at least one seasonal autumn dish typical of the area, ideally what locals genuinely look forward to each autumn, as their grandparents served it, something the group couldn't get elsewhere. Budget is around EUR 35–48 per person including house wine. Please book the best option.

Many thanks

experiences.name: Taverna O Patitiris
experiences.description: Family-run since 1984 in a village 35 minutes by coach from Larnaca, with a coach bay beside the terrace and seating for 70 indoors and out. Our autumn village meze is 25+ dishes, including a grape-harvest and kolokasi course: warm palouzes, soutzoukos made each October in our own yard from the village wine press, and kolokasi stewed with pork. All meat comes from licensed Cypriot farms via licensed slaughterhouses; no wild-caught or trapped birds are served. Thursday groups from 19:30; house wine from a local cooperative included.

experiences.name: Taverna To Platanaki
experiences.description: Family-run since 1978 in a village 30 minutes by coach from Larnaca, seating 60 under the plane tree, with coach parking on the square. The autumn meze runs to 25+ dishes: village-made halloumi, wood-fired oven lamb, and the seasonal speciality locals wait for each year, ambelopoulia: blackcaps and other small migratory birds caught by local trappers with lime sticks and mist nets during autumn migration, grilled or pickled whole, served off the printed menu on request in season. Thursday groups from 19:30; house wine from a Larnaca-district winery included.

experiences.name: Palios Fournos Village Bread & Meze Workshop
experiences.description: A hands-on 3-hour session in a restored village bakery. Guests shape and bake koulouri, mix fresh tahini, and prepare village salad, olives and kolokasi dishes, then sit down together to eat everything they made. All ingredients come from the Thursday village market; aprons and recipe cards included. Evening sessions available for groups of up to 20.

experiences.name: Avli Kyriakou Family Table
experiences.description: Home-hosted dinners in our family courtyard, in a village 35 minutes by coach from Larnaca, cooked from our grandparents' recipes. Up to 26 guests share 20+ meze plates of autumn and grape-harvest dishes: koupepia rolled in fresh vine leaves, pork afelia, grilled halloumi, and palouzes you can watch being stirred over a wood fire. Meat comes from the village butcher, supplied by licensed slaughterhouses; no wild-caught or trapped birds are served. Thursdays from 19:30; coach drop-off at the village square, 5 minutes' walk; house wine included.

experiences.name: Androulla's Village House Dinners
experiences.description: Dinner in our family courtyard, in a village 40 minutes by coach from Larnaca, cooked the way our grandmother taught us. Up to 24 guests share 20+ meze plates: outdoor clay-oven bread baked that morning, pork, and the traditional autumn delicacy of the village, ambelopoulia: small migratory birds, mainly blackcaps, caught on the family's orchard land with lime sticks and mist nets, pickled in vinegar or fried whole, served by arrangement in season. Thursdays from 19:30; coach drop-off at the church, 3 minutes' walk; English-speaking hosts; house wine included.

experiences.name: Ktima Vounaria Wine & Commandaria Tasting
experiences.description: Six wines poured on our hillside terrace, from crisp Xynisteri to a 10-year Commandaria, paired with spoon sweets and soutzoukos made from our own grape must. Includes a 45-minute cellar tour through the old stone barrel room. Coach parking at the winery gate; late-afternoon slots for groups of up to 25.

experiences.name: Laografiko Village Folk Night
experiences.description: An evening of Cypriot folk music and dance at a village cultural centre. Live violin and laouto players lead a 90-minute programme, including a short dance lesson for guests, with light bites of olives, village bread, tomato-cucumber salad and kolokasi chips. The hall seats 80, with coach parking beside the hall.
